|publisher= Bank of Baroda |access-date= 17 November 2023}} }} '''Bank of Baroda''' ('''BOB''' or '''BoB''') is an [[Public sector banks in India|Indian public sector bank]] headquartered in [[Vadodara]], [[Gujarat]]. It is the second largest public sector bank in India after [[State Bank of India]]. Based on 2025 data, it is ranked 455 on the [[Forbes Global 2000]] list.{{cite web |url=https://www.forbes.com/companies/bank-of-baroda/ |title=Bank of Baroda |access-date=3 April 2015 |work=Forbes}}{{cite web |url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2010-07-30/news/27587935_1_loan-book-nim-indian-banks |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140819090750/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2010-07-30/news/27587935_1_loan-book-nim-indian-banks |url-status=dead |archive-date=19 August 2014 |title=Resilience to help Bank of Baroda stay a step ahead of peers|work=Economictimes|date=30 July 2010 |access-date=28 April 2012}}{{Cite web |title=Bank of Baroda becomes second public sector lender to hit ₹1 lakh crore market cap |url=https://www.businessinsider.in/stock-market/markets/news/bank-of-baroda-becomes-second-public-sector-lender-to-hit-1-lakh-crore-market-cap/articleshow/101104397.cms |access-date=2023-06-20 |website=Business Insider}} The [[Maharaja of Baroda]], [[Sayajirao Gaekwad III]], founded the bank on 20 July 1908 in the [[princely state]] of [[Baroda State|Baroda]], in Gujarat.{{cite web |url=http://www.bankofbaroda.com/heritage.asp |title=About us - The Heritage |publisher=Bank of Baroda |access-date=27 March 2013}} The [[Government of India]] [[Nationalization|nationalized]] the Bank of Baroda, along with 13 other major commercial banks of India, on 19 July 1969 and the bank was designated as a profit-making [[Public sector undertakings|public sector undertaking]] (PSU). ==History== [[File:Sayajirao Gaekwad III, Maharaja of Baroda, 1919.jpg|thumb|[[Sayajirao Gaekwad III]], the founder of Bank of Baroda]] [[File:Bank of Baroda International Banking Branch at MG Road, Bengaluru formerly Vijaya Bank Head Office 01.jpg|thumb|Bank of Baroda International Banking Branch at MG Road, Bengaluru formerly [[Vijaya Bank]] Head Office]] In 1908, [[Sayajirao Gaekwad III]], set up the Bank of Baroda (BoB),{{Cite web|url=https://bankofbaroda.bank.in/foundation-day|title=Bank of Baroda Foundation Day|website=bankofbaroda.com|access-date=9 April 2024}} with other stalwarts of industry such as Sampatrao Gaekwad, Ralph Whitenack, Vithaldas Thakersey, Lallubhai Samaldas, Tulsidas Kilachand and NM Chokshi.{{cite web|url=http://www.bankofbaroda.co.in/heroes.asp |title=The Heroes |publisher=Bank of Baroda |access-date=13 September 2013}} Two years later, BoB established its first branch in [[Ahmedabad]]. The bank grew domestically until after World War II. Then in 1953, it crossed the Indian Ocean to serve the communities of [[Indians in Kenya]] and [[Indians in Uganda]] by establishing a branch each in [[Mombasa]] and [[Kampala]]. The next year, it opened a second branch in Kenya, in [[Nairobi]], and in 1956, it opened a branch in Tanzania at [[Dar-es-Salaam]]. Then, in 1957, BoB took a big step abroad by establishing a branch in London. London was the center of the British Commonwealth and the most important international banking center. In 1958, BoB acquired Hind Bank (Calcutta; est. 1943), which became BoB's first domestic acquisition.{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}} ===1960s=== {{Unreferenced section|date=October 2021}} In 1961, BoB acquired New Citizen Bank of India. This merger helped it increase its branch network in [[Maharashtra]]. BoB also opened a branch in [[Fiji]]. The next year, it opened a branch in [[Mauritius]] In 1963, BoB acquired Surat Banking Corporation in [[Surat]], Gujarat. The next year, BoB acquired two banks: Umbergaon People's Bank in southern [[Gujarat]] and Tamil Nadu Central Bank in [[Tamil Nadu]] state. In 1965, BoB opened a branch in Guyana. That same year, BoB lost its branch in [[Narayanganj]] ([[East Pakistan]]) due to the [[Indo-Pakistani War of 1965]]. It is unclear when BoB opened the branch. In 1967, it suffered a second loss of branches when the Tanzanian government nationalised BoB's three branches there at ([[Dar es Salaam]], [[Mwanga District|Mwanga]], and [[Moshi, Kilimanjaro|Moshi]]), and transferred their operations to the Tanzanian government-owned [[National Bank of Commerce (Tanzania)|National Banking Corporation]]. In 1969, the Indian government nationalised 14 top banks, including BoB. BoB incorporated its operations in Uganda as a 51% subsidiary, with the government owning the rest. ===1970s=== {{Unreferenced section|date=October 2021}} In 1972, BoB acquired [[Bank of India]]'s operations in Uganda. Two years later, BoB opened a branch each in [[Dubai]] and [[Abu Dhabi]]. Back in India, in 1975, BoB acquired the majority shareholding and management control of Bareilly Corporation Bank (est. 1954) and [[Nainital Bank]] (est. in 1922), both in [[Uttar Pradesh]] and Uttarakhand, respectively. Since then, Nainital Bank has expanded to [[Uttarakhand]], Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Rajasthan, and Delhi state. Right now, BoB have 99% shareholding in Nainital Bank. International expansion continued in 1976 with the opening of a branch in Oman and another in [[Brussels]]. The Brussels branch was aimed at Indian firms from [[Mumbai]] ([[Bombay]]) engaged in diamond cutting and jewellery having business in [[Antwerp]], a major center for [[diamond cutting]]. Two years later, BoB opened a branch in New York and another in the Seychelles. Then in 1979, BoB opened a branch in [[Nassau, Bahamas|Nassau]], the Bahamas. ===1980s=== {{Unreferenced section|date=October 2021}} In 1980, BoB opened a branch in Bahrain and a representative office in Sydney, Australia. BoB, [[Union Bank of India]], and [[Indian Bank]] established IUB International Finance, a licensed deposit taker, in Hong Kong. Each of the three banks took an equal share. Eventually (in 1999), BoB would buy out its partners. A second consortium or joint-venture bank followed in 1985. BoB (20%), [[Bank of India]] (20%), [[Central Bank of India]] (20%) and ZIMCO (Zambian government; 40%) established [[Indo-Zambia Bank Limited|Indo-Zambia Bank]] in [[Lusaka]]. That same year, BoB also opened an Offshore Banking Unit (OBU) in Bahrain (Gulf). Back in India, in 1988, BoB amalgamated Traders Bank (established in 1947 in Delhi), which had a network of 34 branches in Delhi. The Reserve Bank had mandated the amalgamation. ===1990s=== {{Unreferenced section|date=October 2021}} In 1992, BoB opened an OBU in Mauritius, but closed its representative office in Sydney. The next year, BoB took over the London branches of [[Union Bank of India]] and [[Punjab & Sind Bank]] (P&S). P&S's branch had been established before 1970, and Union Bank's after 1980. The [[Reserve Bank of India]] ordered the takeover of the two following the banks' involvement in the Sethia fraud in 1987 and subsequent losses. [[File:Dubai Creek March 2008 (1).JPG|thumb|A Bank of Baroda branch at [[Dubai Creek]].]] In 1996, BoB Bank entered the capital market in December with an [[initial public offering]] ([[Initial public offering|IPO]]). The government of India is still the largest shareholder, owning 66% of the bank's equity. In 1997, BoB opened a branch in [[Durban]]. The next year, BoB bought out its partners in IUB International Finance in Hong Kong. Apparently, this was a response to regulatory changes following Hong Kong's reversion to the People's Republic of China. The now wholly owned subsidiary became Bank of Baroda (Hong Kong), a restricted license bank. BoB also acquired Punjab Cooperative Bank in a rescue. BoB incorporates a wholly–owned subsidiary, [[BOB Capital Markets]], for broking business. In 1999, BoB merged with Bareilly Corporation Bank as part of another rescue. At the time, Bareilly had 64 branches, including four in [[Delhi]]. In Guyana, BoB incorporated its branch as a subsidiary, Bank of Baroda Guyana. BoB added a branch in Mauritius and closed its Harrow Branch in London. ===2000s=== In 2000, BoB established Bank of Baroda (Botswana). The bank has three banking offices, two in Gaborone and one in Francistown. In 2002, BoB converted its subsidiary in Hong Kong from a deposit-taking company to a Restricted License Bank.{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}} In 2002, BoB acquired Benares State Bank (BSB) at the Reserve Bank of India's request. BSB had been established in 1946 but traced its origins back to 1871 and its function as the treasury office of the Benares state. In 1964, BSB acquired Bareilly Bank (est. 1934), with seven branches in the western districts of Uttar Pradesh; BSB also took over Lucknow Bank in 1968. The acquisition of BSB brought BoB 105 new branches. Lucknow Bank, a unit bank with its only office in Aminabad, was established in 1913. Also in 2002, BoB listed [[Bank of Baroda (Uganda)]] on the [[Uganda Securities Exchange]] (USE). The next year BoB opened an OBU in [[Mumbai]].{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}} In 2004, BoB acquired the failed South Gujarat Local Area Bank. BoB also returned to Tanzania by establishing a subsidiary in [[Dar-es-Salaam]]. BoB also opened a representative office each in [[Kuala Lumpur]], Malaysia, and [[Guangdong]], China.{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}} In 2005, BoB built a Global Data Centre (DC) in [[Mumbai]] for running its centralised banking solution (CBS) and other applications in more than 1,900 branches across India and 20 other countries where the bank operates. BoB also opened a representative office in Thailand.{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}} In 2006, BoB established an Offshore Banking Unit (OBU) in Singapore.{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}} In 2007, its centenary year, BoB's total business crossed 2.09 trillion ([[Long and short scales|short scale]]), its branches crossed 2000, and its global customer base 29 million people. In Hong Kong, the Bank got a Full Fledged Banking license, and the business of its Restricted License Banking subsidiary was taken over by the Bank of Baroda branch in Hong Kong w.e.f.01.04.2007.{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}} In 2008, BoB opened a branch in [[Guangzhou]], China (02/08/2008) and in Kenton, Harrow, United Kingdom. BoB opened a joint venture life insurance company with [[Andhra Bank]] and [[Legal & General]] (UK) called IndiaFirst Life Insurance Company.{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}} In 2009, Bank of Baroda (New Zealand) was registered.{{cite web | url=http://www.barodanzltd.co.nz/page/?id=5 | title=About Us | publisher=Bank of Baroda New Zealand Ltd. | access-date=October 14, 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171014083634/http://www.barodanzltd.co.nz/page/?id=5 | archive-date=14 October 2017 | url-status=dead }} {{as of|2017}} BoB (NZ) has 3 branches: two in Auckland, one in Wellington.{{cite web | url=https://nzbanks.com/branches/bank-baroda-branches-new-zealand | title=Bank of Baroda Branches - New Zealand | work=Banks in New Zealand | date=2017 | access-date=October 14, 2017}} ===2010s=== In 2010, Malaysia awarded a commercial banking licence to a locally incorporated bank to be jointly owned by Bank of Baroda, [[Indian Overseas Bank]], and [[Andhra Bank]].{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}} In 2011, BoB opened an Electronic Banking Service Unit (EBSU) at Hamriya Free Zone, Sharjah (UAE). It also opened four new branches in existing operations in Uganda, Kenya (2), and Guyana. BoB closed its representative office in Malaysia in anticipation of the opening of its consortium bank there. BoB received 'In Principle' approval for the upgrading of its representative office in Australia to a branch. Bob also acquired Mumbai-based Memon Cooperative Bank, which had 225 employees and 15 branches in Maharashtra and three in Gujarat. It had to suspend operations in May 2009 due to its precarious financial condition.{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}} The Malaysian consortium bank, India International Bank Malaysia (IIBM), finally opened in Kuala Lumpur, which has a large population of Indians. BOB owns 40%, Andhra Bank owns 25%, and IOB owns the remaining 35% of the share capital. IIBM seeks to open five branches within its first year of operations in Malaysia, and intends to grow to 15 branches within the next three years.{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}} On 17 September 2018, the government of India proposed the merger of [[Dena Bank]] and [[Vijaya Bank]] with the Bank of Baroda, pending approval from the boards of the three banks, effectively creating the third largest lender in the country.{{cite web |title=Bank of Baroda, Vijaya Bank and Dena Bank to be merged |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/banking/bank-of-baroda-vijaya-bank-and-dena-bank-to-be-merged/articleshow/65844142.cms |website=The Economic Times |access-date=14 March 2019 |date=18 September 2018}} The merger was approved by the Union Cabinet and the boards of the banks on 2 January 2019. Under the terms of the merger, Dena Bank and Vijaya Bank shareholders received 110 and 402 equity shares of the Bank of Baroda, respectively, of face value {{INR}}2 for every 1,000 shares they held. The merger came into effect on 1 April 2019.{{cite web |title=Vijaya Bank, Dena Bank merger with BoB to be effective from April 1; here's the share exchange plan |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/sectors/banks/vijaya-bank-dena-bank-merger-bob-effective-april-1-share-exchange-plan/story/320823.html |website=Business Today |date=21 February 2019 |access-date=14 March 2019}} Post-merger, the Bank of Baroda is the third largest bank in India, after [[State Bank of India]] and [[HDFC Bank]]. The consolidated entity has over 9,500 branches,{{Cite web|url=https://www.bankofbaroda.com/amalgamation.htm|title=Amalgamation of Bank of Baroda, Vijaya Bank and Dena Bank|website=bankofbaroda.com|access-date=2019-04-05}} 13,400 ATMs, 85,000 employees, and serves 120 million customers.{{cite web |title=Bank of Baroda is now third largest lender as Dena, Vijaya merger take effect |url=https://www.livemint.com/industry/banking/bank-of-baroda-is-now-third-largest-lender-as-dena-vijaya-merger-take-effect-1554039881359.html |website=Livemint |access-date=31 March 2019 |language=en |date=31 March 2019}} The amalgamation is the first-ever three-way consolidation of banks in the country, with a combined business of Rs14.82 trillion ([[Long and short scales|short scale]]), making it the third largest bank after State Bank of India (SBI) and ICICI Bank.{{cite news|date=9 October 2018|title=Bank of Baroda, Vijaya Bank, Dena Bank send merger proposal for govt nod|newspaper=Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/banking/bank-of-baroda-vijaya-bank-dena-bank-send-merger-proposal-for-govt-nod/articleshow/66135751.cms|access-date=9 October 2018}} Post-merger effective 1 April 2019, the bank has become the India's third largest lender behind SBI and ICICI Bank.{{Cite web|last=Agarwal|first=Nikhil|date=2019-03-31|title=Dena Bank, Vijaya Bank merges with Bank of Baroda: 10 things to know|url=https://www.livemint.com/industry/banking/bank-of-baroda-merger-vijaya-dena-sbi-hdfc-icici-1554006701387.html|access-date=2019-04-01|website=Mint|language=en}} Bank of Baroda announced in May 2019 that it would either close or rationalise 800–900 branches to increase operational efficiency and reduce duplication post-merger. The regional and zonal offices of the merged companies would also be closed. ''PTI'' quoted an unnamed senior bank official as stating that Bank of Baroda would look to expand in eastern India as it already had a strong presence in the other regions.{{cite web |title=Merger impact: Bank of Baroda looks to rationalise 800-900 branches |url=https://www.livemint.com/industry/banking/merger-impact-bank-of-baroda-looks-to-rationalise-800-900-branches-1558259961723.html |website=Mint |access-date=19 May 2019 |language=en |date=19 May 2019}} == Subsidiaries == === Domestic subsidiaries === Source:{{cite web |url= https://bankofbaroda.bank.in/writereaddata/images/pdf/revised-Details-of-Business.pdf |title= Revised Details of Business - 2019 |website= bankofbaroda.in |publisher= Bank of Baroda |access-date= 17 November 2023}} # BOBCARD LIMITED (it is a wholly owned subsidiary of Bank Of Baroda in the credit card industry). Net Profit for FY 2024-25 was Rs.56.74 crore. # BOB Capital Markets Ltd.: A wholly owned subsidiary of Bank of Baroda,{{cite web|url=http://www.business-standard.com/india/news/bob-capital-to-begin-e-broking-by-march-end/333805/ |title=BOB Capital to begin e-broking by March-end |publisher=Business-standard.com |date=9 September 2008 |access-date=3 February 2011}} it is a [[Securities and Exchange Board of India|SEBI]]-registered [[investment banking]] company based in [[Mumbai]], Maharashtra.{{cite web |url=http://www.bobcapitalmarkets.com/contact-us.asp |title=Contact Us |publisher=BOB Capital Markets Ltd |access-date=3 February 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110226125254/http://www.bobcapitalmarkets.com/contact-us.asp |archive-date=26 February 2011 |url-status=dead }} Its financial services portfolio includes [[initial public offering]]s, [[private placement]] of debts, corporate [[restructuring]], business valuation, mergers and acquisition, [[project appraisal]], [[loan syndication]], institutional equity research, and brokerage. (Lusaka) == Shareholding == {{Unreferenced section|date=October 2021}} The shareholding structure of the bank {{As of|2025|6|30|lc=y}} is as follows:{{Cite web|title=Bank of Baroda Shareholding Pattern|url=https://bankofbaroda.bank.in/-/media/project/bob/countrywebsites/india/shareholders-corner2/2025/25-07/shpq1-website-15-20.pdf|website=Bank of Baroda |access-date=25 October 2025}} {| class="wikitable" !Shareholders !Shareholding % |- |[[Government of India]] |63.93% |- |Mutual Funds |8.61% |- |Foreign Holding |12.27% |- |Indian Public |7.76% |- |Others |7.4% |} ==International presence== [[File:Bank of Baroda countries of operations map.svg|thumb|Bank of Baroda's worldwide operations.]] [[File:Bank of Baroda, Manchester.jpg|thumb|Bank of Baroda, Manchester]] The bank has 107 branches/offices in 24 countries (excluding India), including 61 branches/offices of the bank, 38 branches of its 8 subsidiaries, and 1 representative office in [[Thailand]]. The Bank of Baroda has a joint venture in [[Zambia]] with 16 branches.{{cite web|url=http://www.bankofbaroda.com/int/index.asp |title=India's International Bank - International |publisher=Bank of Baroda |access-date=3 April 2015}} Among the Bank of Baroda's overseas branches are ones in the world's major financial centres (e.g., [[New York City|New York]], [[London]], [[Dubai]], [[Hong Kong]], [[Brussels]] and [[Singapore]]), as well as a number in other countries. The bank is engaged in retail banking via the branches of subsidiaries in [[Botswana]], [[Guyana]], [[Kenya]], [[Tanzania]], and [[Uganda]]. The bank has recently upgraded its representative office in [[Australia]] to a branch and set up a joint venture commercial bank in [[Malaysia]]. It has a large presence in [[Mauritius]] with about nine branches spread out in the country.{{cite web|url=http://www.bankofbaroda.com/mauritius.asp |title=India's International Bank - Branch Locator - Overseas Branches - Mauritius |publisher=Bank of Baroda |access-date=13 September 2013}} The Bank of Baroda has received permission or in-principle approval from host country regulators to open new offices in [[Trinidad and Tobago]] and [[Ghana]], where it seeks to establish joint ventures or subsidiaries. The bank has received [[Reserve Bank of India]] approval to open offices in the [[Maldives]], and [[New Zealand]]. It is seeking approval for operations in [[Bahrain]], [[South Africa]], [[Kuwait]], [[Mozambique]], and [[Qatar]], and is establishing offices in [[Canada]], [[New Zealand]], [[Sri Lanka]], [[Bahrain]], [[Saudi Arabia]], and [[Russia]]. It also has plans to extend its existing operations in the [[United Kingdom]], the [[United Arab Emirates]], and [[Botswana]].{{Citation needed|date=July 2021}} The tagline of Bank of Baroda is "India's International Bank".{{Citation needed|date=July 2021}} ==Affiliates== IndiaFirst Life Insurance Company is a joint venture between Bank of Baroda (44%) and fellow Indian state-owned bank [[Andhra Bank]] (30%), and UK's financial and investment company [[Legal & General]] (26%).{{cite web|author=anurag |url=http://www.banknetindia.com/banking/91120.htm |title=IndiaFirst Life Insurance becomes the 23rd life insurer in India |publisher=Banknet India |access-date=13 September 2011 |url-status = dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111003091723/http://www.banknetindia.com/banking/91120.htm |archive-date=3 October 2011 }} It was incorporated in November 2009 and has its headquarters in Mumbai. |publisher=dnaindia.com |date=26 December 2009 |access-date=28 April 2010}} ==South Africa corruption controversy== On 4 September 2017 the [[South Africa Financial Intelligence Centre]] fined Bank of Baroda {{INR}} 11 million (equivalent to US$837,000) for flouting anti-corruption laws in transactions on accounts owned by the [[Gupta family]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.moneyweb.co.za/news/companies-and-deals/fic-fines-bank-of-baroda-for-flouting-anti-corruption-laws/|title=FIC fines Bank of Baroda for flouting anti-corruption {{INR}}4.2 billion, the bank tried to close the accounts.{{Cite news|url=https://www.businesslive.co.za/bd/companies/financial-services/2017-09-11-how-bank-of-baroda-was-overwhelmed-by-suspicious-gupta-linked-accounts/|title=How Bank of Baroda was overwhelmed by prevent it from closing their accounts.{{Cite news|url=https://www.timeslive.co.za/politics/2017-09-08-september-21-judgment-day-for-guptas-baroda-bank-accounts/|title=Judgment day for Guptas' Baroda bank accounts|last=Cowan|first=Kyle|date=8 September 2017|work=Sunday Times|access-date=2017-09-14|language=en-US}} During February 2018, it was announced that the Bank of Baroda has given notification to the [[South African Reserve Bank]] that it would be exiting the country.{{Cite web|url=https://businesstech.co.za/news/banking/224773/bank-of-baroda-is-leaving-south-africa/|title=Bank of Baroda is leaving South Africa |website=BusinessTech}} The bank played a crucial role in the Gupta family's business dealings.{{cite web|last1=Joseph|first1=Josy|title=India's Bank of Baroda Played a Key Role in South Africa's Gupta Scandal|url=https://www.occrp.org/en/investigations/7696-india-s-bank-of-baroda-played-a-key-role-in-south-africa-s-gupta-scandal|website=The Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project}} According to a report by the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP), the Bank of Baroda allowed the Gupta family to move millions of dollars in alleged corrupt business transactions to offshore accounts.{{cite web|title=BANK OF BARODA PLAYED KEY ROLE IN SA'S GUPTA SCANDAL|url=http://www.corruptionwatch.org.za/bank-baroda-played-key-role-sas-gupta-scandal/|website=Corruption Watch|access-date=24 April 2018}} Although the Bank of Baroda denies the illicit behavior, the documents report that the bank's South African branch issued unapproved loan guarantees, ignored internal compliance efforts, and averted regulators from learning about suspicious transactions in a way that benefited the Guptas’ network. Around 4.5m Rand has circulated around a handful of Gupta-associated companies between 2007 and 2017. Due to the volume of Gupta-owned accounts, the majority of the bank's transactions in [[Johannesburg]] involved Gupta family funds. Reports reveal that inter-company loans provided an untraceable and inexplicable technique used by the Gupta brothers to transfer money from the Bank to various Gupta-owned companies, like Trillion Financial Advisory and Centaur Mining. The [[suspicious activity reports]] (SARs) filed by workers at the Bank of Baroda related to Gupta transactions were often voided by managers and higher-level bank officials. Most SARs failed to reach the [[South African Financial Intelligence Centre]] as a result.{{Citation needed|date=January 2024}} == Controversies == In October 2023, the [[Reserve Bank of India]] directed Bank of Baroda to suspend onboarding new customers on its "bob World" mobile application due to supervisory concerns regarding unauthorized linking of mobile numbers to boost user targets. Following corrective measures and internal disciplinary actions, the RBI lifted the restriction in May 2024.https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/bank-of-baroda-world-app-case-a-detailed-look-at-the-issue-and-the-regulatory-action-it-triggered-11552951.html In July 2026, Bank of Baroda confirmed a data breach involving approximately 1 terabyte of customer files, loan documents, and audit records leaked to the dark web via a compromised employee email account, though core systems remained secure.https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/bank-of-baroda-initiates-forensic-investigation-on-data-breach-that-leaked-critical-customer-information/article71273011.ece ==See also== {{Portal|Banks}} *[[Indian banking]] *[[Indian Financial System Code]] *[[List of banks in India]] ==References== {{reflist}} ==Further reading== * * * {{Cite book|last1=Tripathi|first1=Dwijendra|title=Towards a New Frontier: History of the Bank of Baroda, 1908-1983|last2=Misra|first2=Priti|publisher=Manohar|year=1985|isbn=9780836428827|location=New Delhi|language=en|oclc=12839220}} Tuesdays holidays ==External links== {{Commons category}} * {{Official website|bankofbaroda.bank.in}} {{Banking in India}} {{Nifty 200 companies}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Bank of Baroda| ]] [[Category:Banks established in 1908]] [[Category:Companies nationalised by the Government of India]] [[Category:Companies based in Vadodara]] [[Category:Indian brands]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 1908]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]]

Bank of Baroda (BOB or BoB) is an Indian public sector bank headquartered in Vadodara, Gujarat. It is the second largest public sector bank in India after State Bank of India. Based on 2025 data, it is ranked 455 on the Forbes Global 2000 list.
The Maharaja of Baroda, Sayajirao Gaekwad III, founded the bank on 20 July 1908 in the princely state of Baroda, in Gujarat. The Government of India nationalized the Bank of Baroda, along with 13 other major commercial banks of India, on 19 July 1969 and the bank was designated as a profit-making public sector undertaking (PSU).
